issue.title: fix(presets): recompose surviving skills when a lower preset layer is removed

labels.name: repo-4ececeac
labels.description: Verdict: high-value, important work for Spec Kit — do first

issue.body:
## Description

Removing a preset that is the base, or a middle layer, of another preset's `prepend`/`append`/`wrap` composition leaves the removed preset's content in the active agent's `SKILL.md`. That affects Claude, Codex, Copilot with `--skills`, and other skills-based integrations. `specify preset resolve` reports the new chain, and command-file agents such as Gemini are recomposed onto it. But the skill keeps the removed preset's instructions, so `/speckit-specify` runs content the user just removed.

Reproduction (`alpha` replaces `speckit.specify` with `ALPHA BODY`; `beta` appends `BETA APPENDED`):

```text
$ specify init p --integration claude --ignore-agent-tools --non-interactive && cd p
$ specify preset add --dev ../alpha --priority 5
$ specify preset add --dev ../beta --priority 2
$ specify preset remove alpha
✓ Preset 'alpha' removed successfully
$ grep -c "ALPHA BODY" .claude/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md
1          # main; 0 with this change
$ specify preset resolve speckit.specify
    (top layer from: beta v1.0.0)
    1. [base] core (bundled) → ...
    2. [append] beta v1.0.0 → ...
```

The same steps with `--integration gemini` drop `ALPHA BODY` from `.gemini/commands/speckit.specify.toml` on `main`, so only skills output is stale.

Root cause, in `presets/_manager_skills.py`:

- On removal, `_reconcile_skills()` only revisits the active skills directory when `_unregister_skills()` restored something there (`if extra_skills_dirs is None or active_provenance`).
- The composed skill is owned by the *surviving* composing preset (`beta`), not the removed one, so nothing is restored and the active directory is skipped.
- The recomposed `.composed/<cmd>.md` that `_reconcile_composed_commands()` writes is therefore never rendered into the skill.
- The condition came in with #3459 (`683bfd0`) and moved in the #4747 refactor. Before #3459 the active directory was always reconciled.

The fix:

- `_reconcile_skills()` now records commands whose winning layer composes (strategy other than `replace`).
- After a removal, it also re-renders those skills in the active directory, but only when the `SKILL.md` still carries the winning preset's `metadata.source: preset:<id>` marker. A new helper, `_skills_owned_by_preset()`, does that check.
- A hand-edited skill is left alone, matching the existing protection for non-owned skills during removal.
- The install and rescaffold paths are unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally with `uv run specify --help`
- [x] Ran existing tests with `uv sync && uv run pytest`
- [x] Tested with a sample project (if applicable): the reproduction above with `claude` (on `main` and this branch) and `gemini` (on `main`)

New tests in `tests/specify_cli/presets/test_manager_skills.py`:
- `test_remove_base_preset_recomposes_surviving_composed_skill`: fails on `main` with `assert "Base preset body" not in content`
- `test_remove_middle_preset_drops_its_layer_from_composed_skill`: fails on `main` with `assert "Middle body" not in content`
- `test_remove_base_preset_preserves_hand_edited_composed_skill`: the negative case, guarding the hand-edit protection; passes before and after

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #195849: with block streaming on, when a provider delta ends right after the dot in a decimal or version (`11.` then `65 GiB`), the block chunker treats the dot as a sentence end and emits `11.` as its own block. The coalescer then joins the blocks with a paragraph break, so the user sees `11.` + blank line + `65 GiB`, which also breaks Markdown table rows.

## User Impact

User impact: numbers and versions such as `11.65`, `42.1` and `v2.4.1` are no longer split across block replies. Sentence breaks still work as before, including a sentence that ends exactly at the end of a delta (`Let me read README.md before answering.` still streams before the tool call).

## Why This Change Was Made

`#pickPreferredBreakIndex` matched sentence ends with `/[.!?](?=\s|$)/`. The `$` alternative fires at the end of the streamed buffer, where the next character has not arrived yet. The pattern now still accepts `!`, `?` and a `.` at the end of the buffer, except a `.` right after a digit, which waits for the next character. `.` followed by whitespace is unchanged. A forced drain still emits everything, so nothing is held back at the end of a reply.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (Gateway + Nextcloud Talk channel plugin, local endpoints)

Tested the actual Gateway from source on macOS 27.2 (arm64) using Node v26.7.0. Ran it twice for each scenario. Once with the base of the PR `245cbaf915` (will refer to as before) and once with the PR itself `4068276a63` (will refer to as after). I used separate state dir, config dir and home dir for each run and used a custom port (38789). I used the same config for all runs which can be seen below and corresponds to what is described in the Issue. `blockStreamingDefault: "on"`, `blockStreamingBreak: "text_end"`, `blockStreamingChunk {minChars: 1, maxChars: 1200}` and `blockStreamingCoalesce {minChars: 1, maxChars: 1200, idleMs: 900}`. Enabled the included `nextcloud-talk` channel plugin with `streaming.block.enabled: true`. Used `run-node` to create a `dist/` folder for each worktree before running. The dist chunker had the `/[.!?](?=\s|$)/g` on before and the PR changes on after.

There are two aspects that use a local stand-in:
- **Model:** I used a local scripted OpenAI compatible API on my machine (127.0.0.1) (`api: "openai-completions"`). I have it send one set message split up into deltas. One of these deltas will end with `11.` and the next will start with `65`. You wouldn't be able to get a hosted model to split here.
- **Nextcloud:** Instead of a real Nextcloud Talk server I have a local capture endpoint (127.0.0.1) that will accept messages from the Gateway. It will check the bot signature on each message and keep track of all messages the bot sends.

Message that comes in is a signed Talk `Create` webhook. It gets sent to the Gateway at `/nextcloud-talk-webhook` by a small local script. Everything else is using the Gateway as is. Receiving the webhook, running the agent, subscribing the agent, chunking blocks, coalescing block replies and sending them through the nextcloud-talk plugin (`POST /ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v1/bot/<room>/message`).

The scripted deltas were identical in every run:

```
delta 0 "Control check: this sentence ends at a delta boundary."
delta 1 " Memory: 11."
delta 2 "65 GiB used."
delta 3 "\n\n| 项目 | 数值 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 内存 | 11."
delta 4 "65 GiB |\n| 磁盘 | 42."
delta 5 "1 GB |\n"
delta 6 "\nDone."
```

**Scenario A: 2 s between deltas (longer than the 900 ms coalescer idle window).** These are the messages the Gateway delivered to the Talk endpoint, verbatim:

Before (`245cbaf915`):
```
09:19:45.265Z send#1 signature_ok=True "Control check: this sentence ends at a delta boundary."
09:19:47.207Z send#2 signature_ok=True "Memory: 11."
09:19:49.207Z send#3 signature_ok=True "65 GiB used."
09:19:51.226Z send#4 signature_ok=True "```\n| 项目 | 数值 |\n| ---- | ---- |\n| 内存 | 11.  |\n```"
09:19:53.227Z send#5 signature_ok=True "65 GiB |"
09:19:56.355Z send#6 signature_ok=True "| 磁盘 | 42.1 GB |\n\nDone."
```

After (`4068276a63`):
```
09:17:29.808Z send#1 signature_ok=True "Control check: this sentence ends at a delta boundary."
09:17:33.741Z send#2 signature_ok=True "Memory: 11.65 GiB used."
09:17:40.886Z send#3 signature_ok=True "```\n| 项目 | 数值      |\n| ---- | --------- |\n| 内存 | 11.65 GiB |\n| 磁盘 | 42.1 GB   |\n```\n\nDone."
```

**Scenario B: 0.3 s between deltas (inside the idle window, so the coalescer joins the blocks).** This is the shape reported in the issue:

Before (`245cbaf915`):
```
09:18:21.977Z send#1 signature_ok=True "Control check: this sentence ends at a delta boundary.\n\nMemory: 11.\n\n65 GiB used.\n\n```\n| 项目 | 数值 |\n| ---- | ---- |\n| 内存 | 11.  |\n```\n\n65 GiB |\n| 磁盘 | 42.1 GB |\n\nDone."
```

After (`4068276a63`):
```
09:18:59.573Z send#1 signature_ok=True "Control check: this sentence ends at a delta boundary.\n\nMemory: 11.65 GiB used."
09:18:59.914Z send#2 signature_ok=True "```\n| 项目 | 数值      |\n| ---- | --------- |\n| 内存 | 11.65 GiB |\n| 磁盘 | 42.1 GB   |\n```\n\nDone."
```

**Results from the tests:**
- **Before:** Will send two permanent messages when the stream pauses. One with `11.` and one with `65 GiB`. When combined by the coalescer it results in `11.\n\n65 GiB`.
- **After:** Will send `11.65 GiB` intact in both cases. Text and Table.
- **Control sentence:** When a sentence ends with a `.` and that happens to be where a delta ends. It will still send that sentence at that period on the PR. For scenario A it happened at `09:17:29.808Z` which is roughly `1s` before the next delta came in at `09:17:30.830Z`.

Below is an excerpt from the Gateway logs during the after run for Scenario B. The logs will not contain any message data. There will be one entry for `resolveAgentRoute` for the incoming message and one for each message sent out. I have removed home dir paths and run id.

```
14:48:50.307+05:30 [gateway] http server listening (23 plugins: ... nextcloud-talk, ...)
14:48:51.062+05:30 [nextcloud-talk] [default] starting Nextcloud Talk Gateway webhook route
14:48:56.516+05:30 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=nextcloud-talk accountId=default peer=group:proofroom guildId=none teamId=none bindings=0
14:48:58.043+05:30 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=scripted api=openai-completions model=scripted-delta method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:38801/v1/chat/completions ...
14:48:58.046+05:30 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=scripted ... status=200 ... contentType=text/event-stream ...
14:48:59.579+05:30 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=nextcloud-talk accountId=default peer=group:proofroom guildId=none teamId=none bindings=0
14:48:59.917+05:30 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=nextcloud-talk accountId=default peer=group:proofroom guildId=none teamId=none bindings=0
14:48:59.986+05:30 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=nextcloud-talk chatId=nextcloud-talk:proofroom messageId=proof-msg-1 ... outcome=completed ...
```

**Things not tested:**
- Real Nextcloud Instance and Hosted Model. As stated above I am using local stand-ins for both.
- Other Channels (qqbot from the Issue, Telegram, Discord). The code that chunks blocks and combines them is shared across channels. But I only tested nextcloud-talk.
- Only Tested on macOS. Did not run the Gateway on Linux.
- The reason the table is shown in a codeblock is because the `nextcloud-talk` plugin converts tables to codeblocks by default (Markdown table mode `code`). This is not related to the PR.
- I did not test the separate issue with the separator that is mentioned in #195849 (`"Hello." + " World"` joined with `\n\n`). It is out of scope here.

### In-process repro and tests

The issue's deterministic repro script (feeds the source one character at a time into `EmbeddedBlockChunker`, then through `createBlockReplyPipeline` with the `paragraph` joiner), run from source on `main` at 245cbaf915, Linux, Node 24.22.2.

Before:
```
chunks   : ["| 项目 | 数值 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 内存 | 11.","65 GiB |\n","| 磁盘 | 42.","1 GB |\n"]
delivered: "| 项目 | 数值 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 内存 | 11.\n\n65 GiB |\n| 磁盘 | 42.\n\n1 GB |\n"

```

After:
```

identical: true
```

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-block-chunker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 29 passed.
- New cases "does not split a decimal or version at a streamed delta boundary" stream the issue's table and a prose sentence with `v2.4.1` and `11.65` one character at a time. Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- The other 28 test files that use the block chunker, block-reply pipeline or block chunking config (including the Ollama pre-tool narration streaming test) pass with the fix.
- Test-line budget: 20 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/block-stream-decimal-split.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

issue.title: s2: omit empty indexes and check stream bounds
issue.body:
If you call `WriterAddIndex()` with an empty writer on master it will create an index with no stream identifier. This will error out when decoding `s2: corrupt input`

```go
var dst bytes.Buffer
w := s2.NewWriter(&dst, s2.WriterAddIndex())
_ = w.Close()
_, err := io.ReadAll(s2.NewReader(&dst))
fmt.Println(err)
```

(1) Skip creating empty indexes (ff52aff). `CloseIndex()` will return no index if input is empty. Nonempty output will be the same.

(2) Validate the size of the stream when reading indexes (4ac218d). `Index.LoadStream` will return `ErrUnsupported` if less than 10 bytes and `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` if the stream is smaller then a valid-sized expected index. Empty streams will work if using a forward reader. Empty streams will report a missing index when using a random reader.

Added tests to `s2/writer_test.go` and `s2/index_test.go`. New test cases for reader will fail with `bytes.Reader.Seek: negative position` if run against the previous PR head.

Passed all four build-tag suites and race checks on 1 and 4 CPUs. Passed 100 focused repetitions. `go vet ./...` and `go fix -diff ./...` pass. Only tested on macOS/arm64. Did not run any other os.

comment.body: The four-byte prefix stores the encoded size, so appending the trailer is intentional. The bounds tests exercise the resulting trailer through `LoadStream`.

issue.title: fix: round BigNumbers before choosing the engineering exponent
issue.body:
`format` with `notation: 'engineering'` and a `precision` gives a different result for a BigNumber than for the same number when rounding carries the value up to 1000:

```js
math.format(999999, { notation: 'engineering', precision: 3 })            // '1.00e+6'
math.format(math.bignumber(999999), { notation: 'engineering', precision: 3 }) // '1000e+3', expected '1.00e+6'
math.format(math.bignumber(950), { notation: 'engineering', precision: 1 })    // '1000e+0', expected '1e+3'
math.format(math.bignumber('0.0009996'), { notation: 'engineering', precision: 3 }) // '1000e-6', expected '1.00e-3'
```

The BigNumber `toEngineering` picks the exponent from the unrounded value and only rounds afterwards, so 999.999e+3 becomes 1000e+3 and the mantissa leaves the 1 to 1000 range. The number version already rounds first (fixed for numbers in #1513).

The fix rounds the BigNumber to `precision` significant digits before the exponent is chosen. This is independent of #3730, which changes how the scale factor is built a few lines below.

The new test in `format.test.js` fails on develop with `'1000e+3' !== '1.00e+6'`. With the change, the unit tests pass (6695 passing, 21 pending), as do `test:generated`, `test:types` and `npm run lint`. The one `test:node` failure, the CLI "should interpret scripts" output order, also fails on develop without this change.

## Summary

I ran the code examples in the guides (`docs/*.md`) and the `//=>` JSDoc examples in `src/` against a fresh build of master. I used `TZ=America/New_York`, since the docs say that is the zone they assume, and I froze `Settings.now` where an example shows a fixed date. I also ran them with `TZ=UTC`. Guides:

- `formatting.md`: for `2017-04-20T11:32:00-04:00`, `toISOWeekDate()` returns `'2017-W16-4'` (it said `'2017-W17-7'`), and `toHTTP()` returns `15:32:00 GMT` (it said `03:32:00 GMT`).

- `formatting.md` token table: the header says the examples are for `2014-08-06T13:07:04.054` in America/New_York. The rows for `H`, `Z`, `ZZ`, `ZZZ`, `ZZZZ`, `ZZZZZ`, `a`, `D`, `t`, `X` and `x` did not match that time. They showed things like `+05:00`, `EST`, `AM`, `9/4/2017` and `9:07 AM`. - `parsing.md` token table: the same wrong rows (`Z`, `ZZ`, `ZZZ`, `a`, `D`, `t`), plus `kk`, which said `17` for 2014. `invalidReason` for "August 32 1982" is `'unit out of range'`, not `'day out of range'`.

- `math.md`: `Duration.fromISO('PY23')` gives an invalid Duration. It should be `'P23Y'`.
- `intl.md`: `dt.toLocaleString({ locale: "es", ...DateTime.DATE_FULL })` ignores the locale and returns `'September 25, 2017'`. I changed it to `dt.toLocaleString(DateTime.DATE_FULL, { locale: "es" })`, which returns the Spanish string shown.

- `DateTime#weekday`: the example used `DateTime.local(2014, 11, 31)`, which is invalid (November has 30 days) and returns `NaN`. I used Dec 31, like the `weekYear` example above it, which returns `3`.

issue.title: fix(experimental): match optional params followed by static text in a segment
issue.body:
With the experimental resolver, a file route whose segment starts with an optional param and continues with static text never matches the URL it builds. For `pages/teams/[[teamId]]-b.vue` (path `/teams/:teamId?-b`) the generated matcher is:

```js
new MatcherPatternPathDynamic(/^\/teams\/(?:\/([^/]+?))?-b$/i, ...)
```

```js
pattern.build({ teamId: '123' }) // '/teams/123-b'
pattern.match('/teams/123-b')    // throws MatchMiss, expected { teamId: '123' }
pattern.match('/teams//123-b')   // { teamId: '123' }
```

The legacy matcher matches `/teams/123-b` and `/teams/-b` for the same path. At the root, `[[teamId]]-b.vue` has the opposite problem: `/-b` misses.

`TreeNodeValueParam.re` put the leading slash inside the optional group whenever nothing came before the param in its segment, even if static text came after it, and the tree then added its own `\/` connector. The slash only moves into the group now when the param is alone in its segment (the next sub segment is missing or starts with `/`), which is what the comment above that check describes and what the legacy matcher does.

I added tests to `generated-matcher.spec.ts` for `teams/[[teamId]]-b`, `[[teamId]]-b`, `teams/[[teamId]]-[[otherId]]` and `teams/[[teamId]]+-b`. All four fail on main with `MatchMiss` (for example on `pattern.match('/teams/123-b')`). With the fix, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run -r build`, `pnpm run -r test:types` and `pnpm run -r test:unit` (2064 tests) all pass, and the existing regexp snapshots in `tree.spec.ts` are unchanged.

## Description

`--last` trims committed whitespace before linting. It now removes only the final newline, preserving leading whitespace and trailing spaces as `--from` does.

git commit --allow-empty -m "  feat: leading spaces"

issue.title: s2: omit empty indexes and check stream bounds
issue.body:
If you call `WriterAddIndex()` with an empty writer on master it will create an index with no stream identifier. This will error out when decoding `s2: corrupt input`

```go
var dst bytes.Buffer
w := s2.NewWriter(&dst, s2.WriterAddIndex())
_ = w.Close()
_, err := io.ReadAll(s2.NewReader(&dst))
fmt.Println(err)
```

(1) Skip creating empty indexes (ff52aff). `CloseIndex()` will return no index if input is empty. Nonempty output will be the same.

(2) Validate the size of the stream when reading indexes (4ac218d). `Index.LoadStream` will return `ErrUnsupported` if less than 10 bytes and `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` if the stream is smaller then a valid-sized expected index. Empty streams will work if using a forward reader. Empty streams will report a missing index when using a random reader.

issue.title: fix(presets): recompose surviving skills when a lower preset layer is removed

labels.name: repo-4ececeac
labels.description: Verdict: high-value, important work for Spec Kit — do first

issue.body:
## Description

Removing a preset that is the base, or a middle layer, of another preset's `prepend`/`append`/`wrap` composition leaves the removed preset's content in the active agent's `SKILL.md`. That affects Claude, Codex, Copilot with `--skills`, and other skills-based integrations. `specify preset resolve` reports the new chain, and command-file agents such as Gemini are recomposed onto it. But the skill keeps the removed preset's instructions, so `/speckit-specify` runs content the user just removed.

Reproduction (`alpha` replaces `speckit.specify` with `ALPHA BODY`; `beta` appends `BETA APPENDED`):

```text
$ specify init p --integration claude --ignore-agent-tools --non-interactive && cd p
$ specify preset add --dev ../alpha --priority 5
$ specify preset add --dev ../beta --priority 2
$ specify preset remove alpha
✓ Preset 'alpha' removed successfully
$ grep -c "ALPHA BODY" .claude/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md
1          # main; 0 with this change
$ specify preset resolve speckit.specify
    (top layer from: beta v1.0.0)
    1. [base] core (bundled) → ...
    2. [append] beta v1.0.0 → ...
```

The same steps with `--integration gemini` drop `ALPHA BODY` from `.gemini/commands/speckit.specify.toml` on `main`, so only skills output is stale.

Root cause, in `presets/_manager_skills.py`:

- On removal, `_reconcile_skills()` only revisits the active skills directory when `_unregister_skills()` restored something there (`if extra_skills_dirs is None or active_provenance`).
- The composed skill is owned by the *surviving* composing preset (`beta`), not the removed one, so nothing is restored and the active directory is skipped.
- The recomposed `.composed/<cmd>.md` that `_reconcile_composed_commands()` writes is therefore never rendered into the skill.
- The condition came in with #3459 (`683bfd0`) and moved in the #4747 refactor. Before #3459 the active directory was always reconciled.

The fix:

- `_reconcile_skills()` now records commands whose winning layer composes (strategy other than `replace`).
- After a removal, it also re-renders those skills in the active directory, but only when the `SKILL.md` still carries the winning preset's `metadata.source: preset:<id>` marker. A new helper, `_skills_owned_by_preset()`, does that check.
- A hand-edited skill is left alone, matching the existing protection for non-owned skills during removal.
- The install and rescaffold paths are unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally with `uv run specify --help`

issue.title: Improve scaling calculation in autocontrast()
issue.body:
Changes proposed in this pull request:

 * The `autocontrast()` docstring says the lightest pixel becomes white (255), but the lookup table is built with floats
https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/4d01b943b9550450757968168a32ea03448b5464/src/PIL/ImageOps.py#L182-L185
and `int()` truncates values such as `254.99999999999997` down to 254.

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageOps

im = Image.new("L", (2, 1))
im.putpixel((1, 0), 25)
print(ImageOps.autocontrast(im).getpixel((1, 0)))  # 254, expected 255
```

For 4852 of the 32640 possible (darkest, lightest) pairs, the lightest pixel ends up as 254.

 * The table is now calculated with integers, `(ix - lo) * 255 // (hi - lo)`, which is the exact value of the existing formula rounded down. Across all pairs, 12094 table entries change, 4852 of them the lightest pixel and the rest values in between. Each one is a case where the exact value is a whole number and the float result was 1 below it, so those output pixels are now 1 higher. No entry goes down, and the darkest pixel still maps to 0.
 * Added `test_autocontrast_lightest`. On main it fails with `assert 254 == 255`.

The full test suite, `tox -e lint` and `tox -e mypy` pass locally.

issue.title: ws: accept the IANA registered close codes 1012-1014
issue.body:
`ws.CheckCloseFrameData` rejects the close codes 1012 (Service Restart), 1013 (Try Again Later) and 1014 (Bad Gateway) with `status code is not defined in spec`, because `StatusCode.IsProtocolDefined` only lists the codes from RFC 6455 section 7.4.1. As a result `wsutil.ControlHandler` answers a peer that closes with, say, 1012 by sending a 1002 protocol error close instead of echoing 1012, and returns the protocol error instead of `ClosedError`:

```go
code := ws.StatusCode(1012)
err := ws.CheckCloseFrameData(code, "")
// err == ws.ErrProtocolStatusCodeUnknown, want nil
```

These three codes are in the IANA WebSocket Close Code Number Registry that RFC 6455 section 11.7 creates, and servers do send them (1012 on restart, 1013 when overloaded). coder/websocket accepts all three on receipt, gorilla/websocket accepts 1012 and 1013. Codes that really are unassigned, like 1016 or 2999, are still rejected, so the Autobahn 7.9.x cases are unaffected.

The change adds 1012-1014 to `IsProtocolDefined`, and exports them as `StatusServiceRestart`, `StatusTryAgainLater` and `StatusBadGateway` next to the other status codes, with matching `CompiledCloseServiceRestart`, `CompiledCloseTryAgainLater` and `CompiledCloseBadGateway` frames.

New tests: `TestCheckCloseFrameData` and `TestCompiledClose` in the `ws` package and a 1012 case in `TestControlHandler`. On master they fail with:

```
check_test.go:67: CheckCloseFrameData(1012) = status code is not defined in spec; want <nil>
handler_test.go:146: unexpected error: status code is not defined in spec; want ws closed: 1012 service restart
```

With the change they pass, as do `go test -race -shuffle=on ./...`, `go test -tags purego ./...` and `gofmt -l`. I could not finish `make autobahn` locally (the image pull timed out); the unassigned codes Autobahn 7.9.x checks are still rejected by the new test.

issue.title: ws: reject a Sec-WebSocket-Key that does not decode to 16 bytes
issue.body:
`ws.Upgrader` and `ws.HTTPUpgrader` only check that `Sec-WebSocket-Key` is 24 bytes long, so they answer 101 to keys that are not base64 or do not decode to 16 bytes:

```
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
```

RFC 6455 section 4.2.1 requires "a base64-encoded value that, when decoded, is 16 bytes in length", and says the server must stop processing a handshake that does not match and answer with an error such as 400. The fix decodes the key into a stack array and returns `ErrHandshakeBadSecKey` (400) otherwise. A client that sends such a key (including one in the URL-safe base64 alphabet) now gets 400 instead of 101. Allocations are unchanged; with `-bench 'Upgrader/base$' -cpu=1 -count=10`, benchstat shows `Upgrader/base` 321.0n vs 337.4n and `HTTPUpgrader/base` 1.812µ vs 1.803µ, both `~`; the decode itself takes about 20ns.

Two new `upgradeCases` fail on master in both `TestHTTPUpgrader` and `TestUpgrader`:

```
server_test.go:484: expected error to be 'handshake error: bad "Sec-WebSocket-Key" header', got '<nil>'
```

`go test -race -shuffle=on -cover ./...`, `go test -tags purego ./...`, `make test`, `go vet .` and `gofmt -l` pass.
